Answer: B
Reason: The CT images (Figures 1a-1c) demonstrate diffuse, randomly distributed micronodules throughout the lung parenchyma, which is the hallmark radiographic pattern of miliary tuberculosis. This finding correlates with the clinical history of prolonged fever and increased sedimentation rate, whereas the other options describe patterns (large nodules, peribronchovascular distribution, or centrilobular predominance) not seen in these images.
